questions.q: What does the 5 Second Rule tell you to do?
a: Move physically within five seconds of an impulse to act
Wait five seconds before answering a hard question
Count to five whenever anxiety rises
Plan for five seconds before every task
questions.why: The overview says the brain kills an idea unless you act within five seconds.

questions.q: What are the three reasons the right moment never arrives?
a: Change is new, uncertain and scary
Change is costly, slow and lonely
Change is risky, public and permanent
Change is painful, rare and unpredictable
questions.why: Lesson 2 lists novelty, uncertainty and fear as the constants behind every change.

questions.q: How does the summary describe courage?
a: It compounds through small acts repeated over time
It is a fixed trait some people are born with
It appears suddenly in moments of crisis
It fades unless you attempt bigger risks
questions.why: Lesson 1 compares courage to compound interest, built by many small choices.

questions.q: What did Antonio Damasio's research suggest about decisions?
a: Most of them are driven by feelings rather than facts
Most of them follow careful logical deliberation
Feelings have almost no influence on behavior
People act first and feel nothing afterwards
questions.why: Lesson 3 cites the finding that about 95 percent of decisions come from feeling.

questions.q: What does psychological intervention mean in the summary?
a: Changing your behavior first so your feelings follow
Talking through your feelings before acting
Rewriting negative thoughts before sleep
Avoiding situations that trigger strong emotion
questions.why: Lesson 3 quotes Seneca's idea that doing good leads to feeling good.
